front_blocks.md: Define **partnership agreement**.

back_blocks.md: A **partnership agreement** is a document setting out the **terms on which the partnership operates**.
Its purpose is to help the partners avoid disagreements later on.

cards.front_md: Define **partnership agreement**.
cards.back_md:
A **partnership agreement** is a document setting out the **terms on which the partnership operates**.

Its purpose is to help the partners avoid disagreements later on.

front_blocks.md: Complete the sentence about a partnership agreement:
The agreement states the rate of interest to be paid on partners' `\_\_\_\_\_\_` and the rate to be charged on their `\_\_\_\_\_\_`.

back_blocks.md: The completed sentence is:
The agreement states the rate of interest to be paid on partners' **capital** and the rate to be charged on their **drawings**.

front_blocks.md: Why are partners given interest on their capital?

back_blocks.md: To **reward** them for investing their own money in the business.
A partner who has put in more capital therefore earns more interest.

cards.front_md: Why are partners given interest on their capital?
cards.back_md:
To **reward** them for investing their own money in the business.

A partner who has put in more capital therefore earns more interest.

front_blocks.md: Why is interest charged on partners' drawings?

back_blocks.md: To **discourage** partners from taking money out of the business.
It makes withdrawing money cost the partner something, which is the opposite purpose to interest on capital.

cards.front_md: Why is interest charged on partners' drawings?
cards.back_md:
To **discourage** partners from taking money out of the business.

It makes withdrawing money cost the partner something, which is the opposite purpose to interest on capital.

front_blocks.md: Why might a partner lend money to the business rather than invest more capital?

back_blocks.md: Because a **loan is repayable**, so the money is not tied up in the business, and it gives the partner a guaranteed income from the repayments.
It also avoids having to alter the partnership agreement.

cards.front_md: Why might a partner lend money to the business rather than invest more capital?
cards.back_md:
Because a **loan is repayable**, so the money is not tied up in the business, and it gives the partner a guaranteed income from the repayments.

It also avoids having to alter the partnership agreement.

front_blocks.md: How are losses shared between partners?

back_blocks.md: In the **same agreed ratio** as profits.
The agreement covers the distribution of profits **and** losses, so one ratio serves for both.

cards.front_md: How are losses shared between partners?
cards.back_md:
In the **same agreed ratio** as profits.

The agreement covers the distribution of profits **and** losses, so one ratio serves for both.

front_blocks.md: Which partnership items are kept out of the statement of profit or loss?

back_blocks.md: **Interest on partners' capital**, **interest on partners' drawings**, and **partners' salaries**.
All three are dealt with in the appropriation account instead.

cards.front_md: Which partnership items are kept out of the statement of profit or loss?

**Interest on partners' capital**, **interest on partners' drawings**, and **partners' salaries**.

All three are dealt with in the appropriation account instead.

front_blocks.md: Why is a partner's salary not an expense of the business?

back_blocks.md: Because it is not a payment for work in the way an employee's wage is: it is an agreed way of **dividing the profit** between the partners.
An employee's salary is a genuine expense and does appear in the statement of profit or loss.

cards.front_md: Why is a partner's salary not an expense of the business?

An employee's salary is a genuine expense and does appear in the statement of profit or loss.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Interest on a partner's loan is treated differently from interest on a partner's capital.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Loan interest is a **finance cost**, an expense in the statement of profit or loss. Interest on capital is a **share of the profit** and is dealt with in the appropriation account.

front_blocks.md: A partner lends the partnership \$5000 with loan interest at 5% per annum. How does that appear in the statement of profit or loss?

back_blocks.md: As a finance cost of **\$250**, since \$5000 × 5% = \$250.
It is subtracted after the profit from operations to give the profit for the year.

front_blocks.md: Do the adjustments after a trial balance work differently for a partnership?

back_blocks.md: No, they work exactly as they do for a sole trader.
Depreciation, accruals, prepayments and irrecoverable debts are all dealt with in the same way.

cards.front_md: Do the adjustments after a trial balance work differently for a partnership?
cards.back_md:

front_blocks.md: Define the **appropriation account**.

back_blocks.md: The **appropriation account** shows how a partnership's profit or loss for the year is **divided between the partners**.
It is prepared after the statement of profit or loss, following the terms of the partnership agreement.

cards.front_md: Define the **appropriation account**.
cards.back_md:
The **appropriation account** shows how a partnership's profit or loss for the year is **divided between the partners**.

It is prepared after the statement of profit or loss, following the terms of the partnership agreement.

front_blocks.md: Why is the appropriation account prepared after the statement of profit or loss?

back_blocks.md: Because it starts with the **profit for the year**, which is what the statement of profit or loss produces.
There is nothing to divide between the partners until that figure is known.

cards.front_md: Why is the appropriation account prepared after the statement of profit or loss?

front_blocks.md: Is the appropriation account part of the double entry system?

back_blocks.md: The profit or loss for the year is transferred into it from the statement of profit or loss by a double entry, rather than simply being copied across.

cards.front_md: Is the appropriation account part of the double entry system?
cards.back_md:
**Yes.**

The profit or loss for the year is transferred into it from the statement of profit or loss by a double entry, rather than simply being copied across.

front_blocks.md: Complete the sentence about transferring a profit:
A profit for the year is moved into the appropriation account by `\_\_\_\_\_\_` the statement of profit or loss and `\_\_\_\_\_\_` the appropriation account.

back_blocks.md: The completed sentence is:
A profit for the year is moved into the appropriation account by **debiting** the statement of profit or loss and **crediting** the appropriation account.

front_blocks.md: Why is the interest on drawings added rather than subtracted?

back_blocks.md: Because the account is written from the **business's point of view**, and that interest is money the partners **owe the business**.
It therefore increases the amount available to share out between them.

cards.front_md: Why is the interest on drawings added rather than subtracted?

front_blocks.md: What is subtracted from the profit before the residual profit is found?

back_blocks.md: The **interest on partners' capital** and the **partners' salaries**.
What remains is the residual profit, which is then shared in the agreed ratio.

cards.front_md: What is subtracted from the profit before the residual profit is found?
cards.back_md:
The **interest on partners' capital** and the **partners' salaries**.

What remains is the residual profit, which is then shared in the agreed ratio.

front_blocks.md: The profit is \$30 000, interest on drawings totals \$850, interest on capital \$4250 and salaries \$6000. What is the residual profit?

back_blocks.md: Add the interest on drawings, then subtract the interest on capital and the salaries: \$30 000 + \$850 − \$4250 − \$6000 = \$20 600.

cards.front_md: The profit is \$30 000, interest on drawings totals \$850, interest on capital \$4250 and salaries \$6000. What is the residual profit?
cards.back_md:
**\$20 600.**

Add the interest on drawings, then subtract the interest on capital and the salaries: \$30 000 + \$850 − \$4250 − \$6000 = \$20 600.

front_blocks.md: What is recorded in a partner's capital account?

back_blocks.md: Only the capital the partner has **invested**: the original amount, plus anything put in later, less any capital withdrawn.
Drawings and loans from the partner are never entered there.

cards.front_md: What is recorded in a partner's capital account?

front_blocks.md: Why do partnerships keep a capital account and a current account separately?

back_blocks.md: To keep **permanent** changes apart from **temporary** ones.
The capital account then shows plainly what each partner has invested, which also makes the interest on capital straightforward to calculate.

cards.front_md: Why do partnerships keep a capital account and a current account separately?

The capital account then shows plainly what each partner has invested, which also makes the interest on capital straightforward to calculate.

front_blocks.md: Which entries go on the credit side of a partner's current account?

back_blocks.md: Anything that **increases** what the business owes the partner.
That means the **profit share**, the **interest on capital**, the **interest on a loan**, and a **partner's salary**.

cards.front_md: Which entries go on the credit side of a partner's current account?
cards.back_md:
Anything that **increases** what the business owes the partner.

That means the **profit share**, the **interest on capital**, the **interest on a loan**, and a **partner's salary**.

front_blocks.md: Which entries go on the debit side of a partner's current account?

back_blocks.md: Anything that **decreases** what the business owes the partner.
That means the **loss** for the year, the partner's **drawings**, and the **interest on drawings**.

cards.front_md: Which entries go on the debit side of a partner's current account?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A partner receives cash when they are awarded a salary or interest on capital.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
No money moves at that point. The amount is credited to the partner's **current account**, and they may then take it out as drawings, which is when the bank account is used.

front_blocks.md: What does a debit balance on a partner's current account mean?

back_blocks.md: That the partner has **taken more out of the business than their share of the profits**.
A credit balance means the opposite: they have left part of their share in the business.

front_blocks.md: What is the double entry for awarding interest on a partner's capital?

back_blocks.md: **Debit** the appropriation account and **credit** the partner's current account.
The appropriation account is where the profit is being divided, and the current account is where the partner's share builds up.

front_blocks.md: Complete the sentence about a loan from a partner:

A loan from a partner is not part of their capital account: it is shown as a **liability** in the statement of financial position, and the interest on it is added to their **current** account.

front_blocks.md: How does a partnership's statement of financial position differ from a sole trader's?

back_blocks.md: Only in the **capital section**.
The assets and liabilities are set out in exactly the same way, but each partner's **capital account** and **current account** balances are shown separately.

front_blocks.md: In the capital section, how is a debit balance on a partner's current account shown?

back_blocks.md: In **brackets**, and treated as a **negative** figure when the section is totalled.
It is subtracted rather than added, because that partner owes money back to the business.

cards.front_md: In the capital section, how is a debit balance on a partner's current account shown?

front_blocks.md: Which columns are used in the capital section of a partnership's statement of financial position?

back_blocks.md: One column for **each partner**, and one for the **total**.
Each partner's capital and current account balances go in their own column, and the combined figures go in the total column.

front_blocks.md: A partner's capital account stands at \$12 000 and their current account works out at a debit balance of \$1000. What is their total?

back_blocks.md: The current account balance is written as (1000) and subtracted, so \$12 000 − \$1000 = \$11 000.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The two halves of a partnership's statement of financial position still have equal totals.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The total assets equal the partners' combined capital plus the liabilities, exactly as they do for a sole trader.
